subject: Discovery Recap: Tool-calling & structured output (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery Recap: Tool-calling & structured output (Acme Health)

Hi Olivia — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Happy to adjust anything I missed.

High-level pain points you called out
- Inconsistent structured outputs from current model stack (parsing failures + downstream processor errors).
- Need deterministic JSON for agent workflows (triage routing, eligibility checks).
- Latency spikes during peak hours; wanting predictable P95s for user-facing flows.
- Data classification / PHI handling constraints for some patient workflows.

Current stack (what you mentioned)
- Vendor LLM endpoints behind an internal API gateway + Lambda-based orchestration.
- Postgres backend + existing rule engine for business logic.
- A/B experiments running in prod w/ feature flags.

Success criteria (we sketched together)
- >95% responses validate against a provided JSON schema (deterministic fields + minimal post-processing).
- P95 latency < 500ms for single-turn JSON responses in the primary region.
- Clear audit logs and ability to redact PHI as needed.

What Redwood can help with (next steps)
1) Tech deep-dive: schedule a 60–90m session with your infra and engineering leads to review: agent workflows, expected throughput, and schema enforcement needs.
2) Pilot proposal: small proof-of-value on a single agent flow (triage -> routing) with an evaluation rubric (validation rate, latency, cost).
3) Security: share our SOC2 + PHI handling docs; you can send your questionnaire (I attached our baseline answers and a suggested JSON schema to accelerate validation).

Attachments I included
- proposed_json_schema.json (example schema for the triage agent output)
- acme_security_questions.pdf (our completed baseline answers to your questionnaire)

Immediate asks
- Can you share a sample of the current downstream parser failures (logs or a few anonymized examples)? That will help us tailor the schema.
- Who should we book the technical deep-dive with (names + preferred times next week)?

If it helps, I can propose two slots for the deep-dive. Thanks again — excited about the potential here.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Duncan <sam.duncan@acmehealth.com>, security@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-05-20T18:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Tool-calling & structured output (Acme Health)

Thanks Jordan — this is great and matches our notes. A few clarifications and attachments from our side:

Clarifications
- We currently surface the model output to our UI and then run a proprietary parser. The majority of failures are schema mismatches (missing fields, arrays vs objects).
- Throughput: expected ~40 requests/sec for the pilot flow, with spikes up to 120 req/s during batch windows.
- Cost target: we need to keep the incremental inference cost predictable; open to Redwood's batching suggestions.
- PHI scope: the triage flow will likely include PHI in free text; any storage must be configurable for redaction/retention.

Attached
- acme_architecture.drawio (high-level diagram)
- a few anonymized parser-failure examples pasted below.

Parser-failure examples (anonymized)
> Example 1: expected {"symptoms": ["string"], "urgency": "low|medium|high"} but got {"symptoms": "fever, cough", "urgency": "3"} -> downstream crash on array access.
> Example 2: extra keys like {"notes": "see attached"} cause our mapping layer to drop fields.

Next steps from our side
- I'll loop in our engineering manager Sam and security contact (cc'd) to the technical deep-dive. Sam, can you do Tuesday 5/26 or Thursday 5/28 morning PST?
- Security: please confirm you received our questionnaire; we expect SOC2 + details on audit logs.

Appreciate the quick follow-up.

Best,
Olivia Grant
Director of Product, Acme Health
olivia.grant@acmehealth.com

--

Team — forwarding the Acme Health recap and attachments. Quick asks so we can move fast on the pilot: 

1) Product (Ava) — can you review the attached proposed_json_schema.json and advise whether the schema maps cleanly to our enforcement primitives (required fields, type coercion, validation fallback policies)? Also note PHI-containing free-text fields may need redaction helpers or a redaction API hook.

2) Infra (Marcus) — they expect ~40 req/s baseline, spikes up to 120 req/s. Can you estimate P95 for a single-turn structured output path and note any batching recommendations to hit <500ms P95? Include GPU vs CPU options and cost implications.

3) Security (Stephanie) — they asked for SOC2 + audit log details and configurable retention. I attached their questionnaire; please confirm which items we can fill today vs which require legal.

We're targeting a tech deep-dive next week — Sam Duncan suggested Tue 5/26 or Thu 5/28 AM PST. Let me know availability and I'll propose times.

I'll also prepare a short evaluation rubric (validation rate, latency, cost per call) to use during the pilot.

Thanks — Jordan

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-21T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Discovery Recap: Tool-calling & structured output (Acme Health)

Thanks Jordan — quick responses below. I'll book time with Sam and their engineering manager once Marcus confirms capacity.

Product notes:
- Proposed JSON schema looks sensible from a schema-enforcement perspective. A couple of calls-outs:
  * Make arrays explicit and prefer fixed keys for routing decisions (e.g., {"symptoms": ["string"]}).
  * Add a top-level "metadata" object with "redaction_level": "none|partial|full" to let us signal PHI handling.
  * Suggest providing a thin wrapper in the pilot that rejects (400) any response that fails strict validation; we can relax to "best-effort with warning" later.

Infra notes (Marcus please confirm):
- For single-turn JSON responses at 40 req/s, we should be able to hit P95 ~350ms on our dedicated pools with moderate batching (batch windows ~10–20ms) assuming sequence lengths are <512 tokens.
- Spikes to 120 req/s will require autoscaling or burst capacity; we should size initial pilot for a 2x buffer.

Security notes (Stephanie please confirm):
- We can share SOC2 and audit log docs today; PHI redaction will require configuration in the customer private deployment or an enterprise option for managed retention.

Action items
- Marcus: please send a short note with expected P95 numbers and a recommended config for the pilot by EOD.
- Stephanie: confirm which questionnaire items need legal and which product/security can answer directly.
- Jordan: once Marcus confirms, book the deep-dive for Tue 5/26 10:00 AM PST (tentative).

I'll start drafting the pilot evaluation rubric and a JSON-schema validation checklist.

Ava
Senior Product Manager | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai
